title: Disentangling Sampling from Training Budget in Class-Imbalanced CT Body Composition Segmentation
mechanism: Episodic (class-balanced) batch construction in fully supervised segmentation, with the warning that sampling gains are often a training-iteration confound.
adaptation: Batch of 8: force at least one cell with inactive and one with splice/edge_dark/material, rest random; keep 20k steps. Benchmark rule: report iteration budgets when comparing samplers.
min_experiment: Arm: episodic batches, 5 seeds, 20k steps; baseline SUP100; metric mIoU_rob and inactive IoU; kill if both n.d. Run only if RCS arm is unclear.
evidence: R: 210 CT scans, 9 tissues: full data Dice 0.882 vs 0.878 (equal); low data 0.787 vs 0.758/0.762 mostly from 12x iteration difference; under matched budgets random sampling overfits about 3x earlier.

alt_notes.adaptation: Batches of 8 with at least 2 crack, 2 inactive and 1 rare-structure cell; compare at matched 20k steps (already our protocol) and report val overfitting curves.
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF+EP vs PF+RCS vs PF in one sweep; same metrics and kill as RCS.

alt_notes.adaptation: Each batch of 8 holds at least 1 of the 42 inactive cells and spans at least 3 of the 5 sources; compare at matched 20k steps and at 40k; keep it moderate given the crack sampling result.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: PF + episodic batches, 5 seeds. Baseline: SUP100-PF. Metric: inactive IoU (test, E1), BMRK crack/inactive IoU. Kill: inactive IoU gain < 0.02 and BMRK not better.
